summary.intent: Prove that a committed fix for the CipherBox recipient-pin-lifecycle §5 gap (web file-grant re-mint on rotation) actually works end-to-end via the sdk-e2e suite, then decide next steps once the e2e surfaced deeper architectural problems.
summary.outcome: Discovered the seam fix was inert: a genuine base64/hex encoding bug (Gap C) blocking all grant re-mint PATCHes, and a genuine file-leaf key-recovery gap (Gap B) blocking file rotation on web. Gap C was fixed and tested; Gap B was scoped as too large/risky to cram into the PR; the web seam wiring was reverted to dormant; and a research-goals document for a grants-in-relay vs grants-in-metadata architecture decision was written and slated for commit alongside the Gap C fix.

repo: sdk-core rotation engine's reMintGrantsRootedAt (engine.ts:648) encoded re-wrapped keys as base64, but PATCH /shares/:id/grant's UpdateGrantDto requires even-length hex (regex /^(?:[0-9a-fA-F]{2})+$/) — same hex convention as the share-CREATE DTO and Rust's re_mint_grants_rooted_at (engine.rs:704, explicitly commented 'must be hex, NOT base64'). TS was the outlier; web's owner-reconcile.service passed the value through verbatim so every re-mint PATCH 400'd in production.

Web's nodeKeySource (client.ts:2115) only reads folderTree, which is folder-only (lazy DFS) and tracks no parent chain — so it can never resolve a file leaf's ipnsPrivateKey/writeKey during rotation. rotateOne's D-01 guard (engine.ts:1090/1095) throws before mintFileKeyOnRotate for any file child, meaning scope-exit rotation of any shared folder containing files currently fails closed on web (desktop/FUSE is unaffected since Rust resolves keys per-node via a host deps trait, not a pre-supplied map).

v3 data model: writeKey is a per-node symmetric AES key that seals NodeWriteBody = {ipnsPrivateKey, writeChildren, recipientPins}; ipnsPrivateKey is the actual Ed25519 IPNS signing authority nested inside that sealed body. writeChildren (WriteChildRef.writeKeySealed) forms a write-plane key-derivation chain mirroring the read-plane's SealedChildRef.readKeySealed, so one ECIES-wrapped root writeKey grants write access to an entire subtree without per-node per-writer wraps.

Read rotation mints a new readKey but keeps ipnsPrivateKey/writeKey/IPNS name stable (cheap, pointer-stable); write rotation mints a brand-new ipnsPrivateKey and IPNS name, then tombstones the old name — necessary because a writer who already extracted the old ipnsPrivateKey can only be excluded by changing the signing identity itself, not by rotating a wrapping key.

File shares carry no recipientPins (files structurally can't hold pins — 'the file-share carve-out'), so file grants are pin-exempt on re-mint while folder grants are fail-closed verified against owner-sealed pins. This asymmetry is the structural root of Gaps B/C: a file shared independently of its parent folder (e.g. folderA/b.txt shared directly to Darren/Eugene) is rekeyed as collateral damage whenever any covered mutation triggers rotation of the containing folderA subtree, yet has no pin protection and (until Gap C) no working re-mint path at all.

A revoke (DELETE /shares/{id}) is lazy/decoupled from rotation per ADR-0002: it deletes the relay row immediately but does not rotate keys, so the revoked party's already-held readKey remains cryptographically valid for folder content until the next covered mutation triggers rotation — revocation is enforced only at the next rotation, never retroactively.

A likely sibling of the Gap C bug exists at engine.ts:2833 in rotateWriteFromNode (write-plane grant re-mint, encryptedWriteKey) but was left unfixed/flagged since it's out of the read-rotation §5 scope and Rust has no visible write-plane grant re-mint twin to check parity against.
tests/sdk-e2e has no typecheck script; running tsc directly against it was necessary to validate the dormant-seam revert.
workflow: Delegating heavy iterative work (standing up a full local docker stack, authoring a red→green e2e test, running it against live infra) to a background Agent while continuing to gather SDK specifics and write context in parallel kept the main context clean while the agent worked ~22 minutes / 83 tool calls.

After a delegated agent reports findings, the agent's claims were independently re-verified against the actual branch code (reading engine.ts, checking Rust engine.rs for parity, grepping the DTO validator) before presenting them to the user as fact — did not take the subagent's report on faith.

When a subagent's fix touches files whose removal would break another artifact (the skipped e2e test referencing resolveInlineGrantRemint on RotationClientCallbacks), the resolution was to keep the interface as a dormant opt-in hook rather than deleting it outright, preserving typecheck-cleanliness for downstream consumers.

When a user's clarifying questions repeatedly complicate the fix's scope, the right move was pausing implementation for two rounds of AskUserQuestion and ultimately writing a standalone research-goals document rather than continuing to code against a decision that hadn't been made yet.

friction: Local dev stack (Docker daemon, API, postgres/redis/kubo/mock-ipns-routing) was completely down at session start, requiring bringing up the full stack before any e2e work could run, adding significant setup latency.

A combined Bash command reading sdk-e2e README + .env was denied by the sandbox (likely due to touching .env); had to fall back to separate, narrower reads and use a known secret already stored in memory instead of reading .env directly.

Locating WriteChildRef's fields and the IPNS-key-from-writeKey recovery pattern required several rounds of grep/read (client.ts, multiple engine.ts passes) before the mirror-target code (client.ts:5584-5596, updateSharedFile) was found.

The background agent could not fully fix the gaps it found (Gap B, Gap C) because its task scope was test-only (tests/sdk-e2e), so it committed a describe.skip reproduction instead — requiring the main session to pick the fixes back up manually.
open_items: Gap B (file-leaf IPNS/write key recovery during rotation on web) remains unfixed — assessed as a phase-sized, design-and-review change touching the hottest zeroization-sensitive code path in the engine (previously broke 48/89 E2E tests); deferred pending the architecture decision from the research sprint.
engine.ts:2833 (write-plane rotateWriteFromNode, encryptedWriteKey) flagged as a probable sibling of the Gap C base64/hex bug but left unfixed and unverified against Rust parity.
The skipped sdk-e2e file-grant-remint test (tests/sdk-e2e/src/suites/file-share-rotation-remint.test.ts, commit 680344873) is committed but not pushed; needs to be driven red→green once Gap B lands.
Local infra stack (postgres/redis/kubo/someguy/mock-ipns-routing + API on :3000) was left running after the background agent's work, not torn down.

Research goals document at .planning/research/grant-delivery-rotation-research-goals.md needs a follow-up research/prototyping sprint to decide grants-in-relay (fix Gap B/C) vs grants-in-metadata (architecture change that would eliminate Gap B/C structurally) before further #615 work proceeds.

PR #615 reshaping (revert web's live seam usage in owner-reconcile.service.ts and rotation-driver.service.ts, keep Gap C fix, keep skipped e2e, commit research doc) was in progress at transcript end — commits for Gap C, the web pullback, and the research doc were being created as three separate logical commits.
